title: Winnecroscoms Neck (Mastic)
summary: Winnecroscoms is a neck of land in Brookhaven town, one of the necks into which Mastic was divided. Related forms include Winocrosscombs, Wenacroscoms, Wenicroscoms, Winecroscum, and Wannuggeashcum.
history_content: The name is tied to Mastic land records, historical geography, and Unkechaug people in the late seventeenth century. Its exact neck boundary remains uncertain, with only a broad association to the Mastic Peninsula.
translation_content:
The name is treated as personal, belonging to an Indigenous owner or dweller rather than giving a separate landscape translation.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names studies can be a wonderful way for an Indigenous organization to record important, timely, and vital information.”

— Alestine Andre, Ingrid Kritsch, Kristi Benson, and Sharon Snowshoe, An Indigenous Place Names Handbook: Sharing the Gwich’in Experience in Canada (2023), Executive summary, printed p. vi; PDF page 7

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: The placename is connected with documented Unkechaug presence and the complex record of Mastic necks, while uncertain boundaries remain approximate.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement on the Mastic Peninsula in Brookhaven. Coordinates are a broad modern anchor and not exact deed boundaries.
